key_insight: COVID-19 was associated with higher rates of cognitive impairment and dementia, with larger early increases among unvaccinated people and persistent elevations reported up to four years.
clinical_relevance: The findings highlight persistent cognitive concerns after COVID-19, particularly among people who were unvaccinated or hospitalised.
method: Analysed linked OpenSAFELY-TPP health records from 18.3 million adults registered with English GPs.
Compared pre-vaccination, vaccinated and unvaccinated cohorts with up to 5.5 years of follow-up.
Estimated adjusted hazard ratios for neurological diagnoses after COVID-19 versus before or without COVID-19.
evidence_signal: During weeks 0–4, adjusted hazard ratios for cognitive impairment/dementia were 2.24/2.05 in vaccinated people and 4.38/8.69 in unvaccinated people.
watch_item: These observational associations do not establish causation or isolate vaccination effects from differences between cohorts.
paper_title: Association of COVID-19 with neurodegenerative and neurological disorders in vaccinated and unvaccinated people
